summary: Son of Bull Smith, with a home lot at Nissequogue and land at the Northeast Branch in Smithtown; John's 9th-great-grandfather.
bio:
Job Smith was born about 1647, a son of Richard "Bull" Smith, the patentee of Smithtown, and his wife Sarah. He married Elizabeth, daughter of John Thompson of Setauket. He lived with his brothers at Nissequogue, where the home lots ran in order from Jonathan's to Richard's to "the home lot of Job Smith". On 30 August 1688 his parents settled land by deed on Job and on his sons Job, Richard, Joseph and Timothy, giving Job himself fifty acres "at the northeast branch, adjoining to the land in the occupation of Daniel Smith"; the Northeast Branch forms the north edge of Hauppauge Neck. He died about 1719.

His children were Job 2d, born 9 March 1679, "Saint" Richard, Timothy, Aaron, the father of Abner Smith (1734–1782), James, Joseph and Elizabeth, said to have been the second wife of the Rev. Daniel Taylor. The Nissequogue homestead passed down to Job Smith 3d, whose son Woodhull Smith sold it; he may be the Woodhull Smith who subscribed to the Hauppauge Methodist church fund in 1806. Through Job 2d's children Anna, wife of Ebenezer Smith, and Epenetus, Job's great-granddaughters became mistresses of the Hauppauge Smith estate, which makes Judge Joshua Smith and Senator Joshua B. Smith John's 3rd cousins 7x removed, assuming that Elizabeth Thompson was the mother of both Job 2d and James. Some family records give James's father as Job's brother Adam, born 1649, but the evidence favours Job. He was John's 9th-great-grandfather.

researchNotes:
Lived with his brothers at Nissequogue, where the home lots ran Jonathan's, then Richard's, then 'the home lot of Job Smith' (Pelletreau Intro. pp. xii–xiii). His father's 1688 deed gave him 50 acres 'at the northeast branch, adjoining to the land in the occupation of Daniel Smith' (pp. 58–59); the Northeast Branch forms the north edge of Hauppauge Neck. His Nissequogue homestead descended to Job Smith 3d, 'and his son Woodhull Smith sold it' (pp. 330–331) — possibly the 'Woodhull Smith' who subscribed to the 1806 Hauppauge Methodist church fund (unproven). Children include James, Job 2d and Aaron (father of Abner Smith, 1734–1782). Through Job 2d's children Anna (wife of Ebenezer Smith) and Epenetus, Job's great-granddaughters became mistresses of the Hauppauge Smith estate, making Judge Joshua Smith and Sen. Joshua B. Smith John's 3C7R. Caveat: the Job-line cousin paths assume Elizabeth Thompson mothered both Job 2d and James. TREE vs PDF: tree shows James's father as 'Justice, A Smith' 1649–1726 (Smithtown 350th logo image); the uploaded PDF gives 'Job Smith + Elizabeth Thompson c. 1647–c. 1719 — 9th great-grandfather'. A 1649 birth matches Bull Smith's son Adam (b. 1649, named in William Hammond's will), so the tree likely attached the wrong son.

Pelletreau prints the 30 Aug 1688 deeds by which Richard 'Bull' Smith and his wife Sarah settled land on Job and on Job's sons Job, Richard, Joseph and Timothy ([R4-S2]). These are near-primary proof of Job's parentage and of the eldest sons' order. The Appendix (pp. 478-479) gives the full list of Job's children: Job 2d (b. 9 Mar 1679), 'Saint' Richard, Timothy, Aaron, James, Joseph and Elizabeth (said to be the second wife of Rev. Daniel Taylor). His wife is Elizabeth, daughter of John Thompson of Setauket ([R4-S1]). Pelletreau puts Job's death 'about 1719' in the Appendix and 'before 1720' in the Introduction ([R4-S1], [R4-S3]). Weygant (1897) gives the same seven children ([R4-S4]).
